title: How many stickers were there at the start?
description: {{NAME_8}} doubles some stickers and gives away five, then doubles again and gives away five, ending with thirteen. A letter for the start gives four ex take away fifteen, and the equation shows seven stickers. Keeko doubts the second round and forgets to double the five.
teaching_notes: One idea: let a letter be the start, write what is left after each round, and set the last expression equal to thirteen. Watch for students who double only the letter and not the five inside the bracket.

source: Asha has some stickers. She doubles them and gives away 5, t
video_script.why: The child sees how a letter for the starting number follows two rounds of doubling and giving away, and how the final count gives an equation.
video_script.substitution: Let x be the start, round one leaves 2x − 5, round two leaves 2 (2x − 5) − 5 = 4x − 15, set 4x − 15 = 13, solve, and check.
video_script.anchor: a row of stickers for the start, a double and give away five round, then the same round again, ending with thirteen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko doubles only the two ex in round two and leaves the five inside the bracket undoubled, so round two seems to leave four ex take away ten.

names.{{NAME_8}}: the child who has the stickers

maths_rules: let x be the start; round one: 2x − 5
slip: 4x − 10 = 13 gives 4x = 23, which is not a whole number
video_script.design: One idea: a letter for the start follows each round, and the end count makes the equation. The rounds stay on the board. Keeko's doubt is that only the letter is doubled.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a row of stickers, then two rounds of double and give away 5, ending with 13 stickers

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.start: the row of stickers appears for the start
marks.rounds: the double and give away 5 round is shown twice
marks.ask: 13 left and the words how many at the start? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>Your book uses letters for unknown numbers to explain tricks and puzzles. Here is one.
<bookmark mark='start'/>{{NAME_8}} has some stickers.
<bookmark mark='rounds'/>{{NAME_8}} doubles them and gives away five, then doubles again and gives away five more.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Thirteen stickers are left. How many did {{NAME_8}} have at the start?

beats.on_screen: the two rounds stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: doubles = 2 times; gives away 5 = take away 5; a letter x stands for the start

marks.plan: a box with the letter x stands for the start
marks.ops: doubles is marked as times 2 and gives away 5 as minus 5

narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>The start is not known, so a letter can stand for it.
<bookmark mark='ops'/>Doubling means two times, and giving away five means taking five away.

beats.on_screen: Given: two rounds of double and give away 5; 13 stickers are left

marks.given: the two rounds and the 13 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two rounds of doubling and giving away five, and thirteen stickers left at the end.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of stickers at the start

marks.find: the words stickers at the start are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of stickers at the start.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: let x = the stickers at the start; after round one: 2x − 5

marks.let: x is written as the stickers at the start

narration: <bookmark mark='let'/>Step one, let ex be the number of stickers at the start.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Round one doubles it to two ex, and giving away five leaves two ex take away five.

marks.double: round one's 2x − 5 is placed in a bracket and doubled

beats.colours: the bracket in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='double'/>Step two, round two doubles everything we have, which is two times, two ex take away five.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Open the bracket. Two times two ex is four ex, and two times five is ten.
<bookmark mark='away'/>Then take away five more, so we have taken away fifteen in all.

marks.add: 15 is added to both sides to give 4x = 28

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step three, thirteen are left, so four ex take away fifteen is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add fifteen to both sides, and four ex is twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Divide twenty eight by four, and ex is seven.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, check with seven. Seven doubled is fourteen, and fourteen take away five is nine.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Nine doubled is eighteen, and eighteen take away five is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The start was seven stickers.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the rounds
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 4x − 10 = 13 and 4x = 23; 23 ÷ 4 is struck out; the bracket 2 (2x − 5) glows with both parts doubled

marks.test: 4x = 23 is written and marked as not a whole number
marks.fix: the bracket glows with 2 × 2x and 2 × 5 both written

beats.colours: the wrong idea in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks round two leaves four ex take away ten, by doubling only the two ex.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Then four ex would be twenty three, which is not a whole number of stickers.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The bracket holds both parts, so the five must be doubled too.
